sources.title: Semaev 2015 t = 2 rows: exact first fall degree and Macaulay degree

nodes.label: Semaev: first fall degree of S_3(x1,x2,z) systems 'always 4'
nodes.statement: For the Weil descent of S_3(x_1, x_2, z) with z a constant (deg_F2 = 2), 'the first fall degree for such polynomials was bounded by 5 in [11]. The experiments show it is always 4 again.'
nodes.scope: Refuted: the first fall degree is 2 (trace identity; 200/200 instances on Semaev's t = 2 cells). Semaev uses this to support Assumption 1 and the first fall degree assumption for the chain system (4).
assumptions: Semaev's definition of first fall degree (Section 4.4)
source_locations: Semaev 2015, Section 4.5 (paragraph on S_3(x_1, x_2, z))

nodes.label: Semaev t = 2 rows: degree needed to prove no solution is 2 or 3
nodes.statement: On 200 instances of Semaev's t = 2 cells (none solvable in V x V), the least Macaulay degree D with 1 in the Boolean span {red(mu [S_3]_j) : deg mu <= D - 2} is 2 on 154 and 3 on 46, never 4; each with a recomputed combination equal to 1. Per cell (sparse / random field polynomial): (15,4) 18/2, 19/1; (15,5) 20/0, 20/0; (16,4) 18/2, 20/0; (19,3) 6/14, 4/16; (21,3) 15/5, 14/6 (degree 2 / degree 3).
nodes.scope: The systems are overdetermined: their quadratic parts depend on x_1 x_2 in a (2k - 1)-dimensional space with 2k - 1 < n. Boolean Macaulay/XL degree, not F4's step trace.

edges.statement: Tr(z^-2 S_3) = Tr(x_1) + Tr(x_2) + Tr(B z^-2): a constant-multiplier fall at degree 2; checked on 200/200 instances.
The degree the systems require is 2 or 3, not Magma's reported 4; the sharp first-fall assumption fails on 46/200 instances (3 > 2).
Consistent with d_F4 <= 4 on the t = 2 rows (degree needed <= 3).
Semaev's support for Assumption 1 cites first fall degree 4 for S_3(x_1, x_2, z); that support is gone, though the d_F4 <= 4 data stand on their own.
